messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P12345 triggered — unusual DNS latency amplification observed for GeoDNS in eu-west-1. Route53 health-check oscillation correlated with increased resolver RTTs. Alerting oncall.
eric: I have the page, jumping in. seeing p95 latency to our api-rw-eu edge jump from ~80ms to 2.6s for a subset of prefixes. errors up ~0.3%.
eric: quick triage: traceroutes show extra hop through resolver pool A (route53 upstream) that intermittently returns SERVFAIL then large TTLs causing clients to fallback and re-resolve.
eric: dig output (sample)
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai A +trace
;; global options: +cmd
;; GOT answer: header: opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 2, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.redwood.ai.                IN      A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai.         60     IN      A       3.120.45.33
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood.ai.             300    IN      NS      ns-1.awsdns-xx.com.
;; WARNING: recursion failed; attempting alternate resolver gave SERVFAIL intermittently
```
ashley: @eric good catch — can you confirm if Route53 health checks are flapping? if so we should temporarily prefer Cloudflare endpoints in GeoDNS or add a fallback policy.
eric: Confirmed — Route53 health-check logs show probes toggling healthy/unhealthy ~every 30-90s for eu-west-1 origin set. suspect transient latency from upstream resolver region.
eric: Impact: EU customers see increased API tail latency, some streaming sessions reset. estimated affected requests ~0.6% of total EU traffic in last 10m (~3k requests).
paul: Suggestion: modify our GeoDNS policy to prefer Cloudflare raw resolvers for eu-west-1 and reduce TTL to 60s so the change propagates quickly. Also disable the flaky Route53 health check temporarily to stop oscillation-driven policy flips.
ashley: Agreed. steps I'm going to run (AWS CLI):
```bash
# lower TTL on geo record
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456789 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"SetIdentifier":"geo-eu","Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.120.45.33"}]}}]}'
# update traffic policy to prefer cf endpoints (pseudo)
aws route53 update-traffic-policy-instance --id tpi-abcdef --ttl 60
```
eric: I'll hold on disabling health check until we have the cf preference ready, to avoid flip-flopping during the update.
luis: prepping status page message draft, will update once we confirm mitigation.
product-alerts-bot: Notifying customers in eu-west via status.redwood.ai/incidents/P12345 (draft ready).
maria: Maria volunteering to own postmortem. please add logs and health-check timeseries to the ticket.
eric: Running a Cloudflare cache purge on edge proxies for the geo record too (curl to API):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$ZONE/purge_cache" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"purge_everything":false, "files": ["https://api.redwood.ai/"]}'
```
ashley: Update: I've pushed the traffic policy change to prefer Cloudflare endpoints for eu-west-1 and set TTL=60. routing now shows >95% to cf-resolvers.
eric: Observing p95 drop back down to ~120ms within ~90s. errors dropping. keeping monitoring for a full 15m.
luis: Published customer note: "We experienced elevated API latency for EU customers due to DNS routing instability affecting eu-west-1. Traffic has been redirected to alternate resolvers; latency normalizing. We’ll post a follow-up with root cause."
eric: Handoff: @ashley taking on cleanup/verify for the next 30m. If any re-flap, escalate to network infra (cc @paul).
ashley: Acknowledged — will keep this thread live, watching health-checks and propagation metrics. I'll also open a support case with AWS for the Route53 health-check flapping.
paul: Logging remediation steps in incident ticket INC-2025-234. Recommendations for postmortem: 1) make geo-policy changes atomic with health-check suspend by default when flips exceed threshold, 2) add synthetic probes to upstream resolvers, 3) evaluate Route53 vs CF health-check stability.
maria: I'll run the postmortem template and schedule follow-up to assign action items; tentative owner: maria. ETA: initial draft in 48h.
eric: Closing note before handoff: primary mitigation = prefer CF, TTL lowered for fast failover, Cloudflare purge run, Route53 health-check suspended if flapping persists. impact window ~10:12–10:18 UTC.
ashley: Marking as monitoring. will update last_message_ts after 15m observation. :white_check_mark:
